title: Do You Need Another Measles Shot?
summary:
The United States lost its measles-free status this week. Mexico and Bolivia lost theirs too, after outbreaks that would not stop.

So do you need another shot? For most people, doctors say no. Most people have had the shots or had measles as kids.

Two shots of the MMR vaccine give the best protection. MMR stands for measles, mumps and rubella. The shots usually protect people for life. People born before 1957 are thought to be immune, because almost everyone caught measles.

Some people should think about a booster: health care workers born before 1957 who cannot prove they are immune, and adults who got shots between 1963 and 1967, when some children got a weaker shot. Doctors say they should get at least one dose of the shot used today. One dose works 93 percent of the time. Two doses work 97 percent of the time.

Not sure how many shots you had? Ask your parents or your doctor.

A booster will not hurt you, doctors say, unless you should not get the shot, like pregnant women.
why_it_matters: Knowing if you are protected from measles helps keep you and your classmates safe at school.

background_read: Measles is a sickness that spreads very easily from person to person.
The MMR shot protects against measles, mumps and rubella, and it usually protects a person for life.
A country loses its measles-free status when outbreaks start again and the sickness spreads.
